## Appearance

Pembroke is a tall woman who has dark hair and dark eyes. She also features a wrinkled cheek.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Nell’s Life P31](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0031)_

## Personality

Mrs. Pembroke is characterized by her unreasonable and stubborn nature. Despite these traits, she remains extremely firm when it comes to her children.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XVI. ## History

Mr. Pembroke resided at a property called [Pear Hill](../codex/places.md#pear-hill). When [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) broke her ankle in a fall at a party hosted by his daughter Isolde, he carried [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) home to [Thirza Abernethy](../character/thirza-abernethy.md). He later drove [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde to [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood) so they could visit [Aunt Lavinia](../character/aunt-lavinia.md) Pembroke for the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition), and he eventually picked the girls up to bring them back home.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Obed Abernethy Is Surprised P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. ## Quotes

> "and I am unable to stop her, because her father encourages and helps her. A book is something she is constantly reading. Having the possibility of a playmate makes me happy—maybe she will spend more time outside because of it."
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022)

> “It’s the most delicious I’ve ever tasted,” Isolde remarked. “It is far better than the one Mrs. Sowerby makes, despite how much she boasts about her own. The flavor is completely different from hers.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Isolde Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P26](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0026)

> "Oh, Nell, regardless of how she got to that place, it was Aunt Lavinia. Oh, and her anger is bound to be immense, I am sure. It’s terrible—it truly is terrible—yet Nell, have you ever encountered a thing quite this amusing?"
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)

> “Is it probable that I would act in that way?” Isolde asked with righteous contempt. “Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)

> “Well, she is inside the room,” Isolde stated. “If you wish to, you may enter. I would not have the courage. Furthermore, I do not think you will accomplish anything at all.”
>
> — Pembroke — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P75](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0075)

## Relationships

### [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/isolde-pembroke--pembroke.md)

Pembroke is the mother of [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md). Isolde first introduced [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) to her family after the two girls met and bonded at [Pear Hill](../codex/places.md#pear-hill), and she later hosted the party where [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) accidentally broke her ankle.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Obed Abernethy Is Surprised P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Nell’s Bringing-up Is Begun P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P0](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0000), +17 more_
